sections.heading: 8. Check your understanding
sections.html:
A design says "the service uses the client credentials grant, so it authenticates with a client secret". What is wrong with the sentence?

It treats two choices as one. The client credentials grant is how the client obtains a token. The client authentication method is how it proves which client it is, and any method can be used with that grant, including private_key_jwt and mutual TLS. Ask which method is registered, and what an attacker would need in order to use it.

A server validates client assertions exactly as RFC 7523 section 3 requires. An attacker copies one assertion from a log 20 seconds after it was made. What happens?

It may well be accepted. RFC 7523 requires the signature, iss, sub, aud and exp checks, and the copy passes all of them until it expires. Tracking jti is optional in that RFC. OpenID Connect Core section 9 requires single use. Check 11 of the lab is the first server and check 10 is the second.

An API returns 401 with error="insufficient_user_authentication" and max_age="300". The client refreshes its access token and retries. Does that work?

No. RFC 9470 section 6.1 says auth_time and acr are set when the user authenticates and do not change when a token is renewed. The client has to send the user through a new authorization request that carries max_age=300, so that the authorization server authenticates the user again.

A vendor says its payments API is FAPI 2.0 certified. Name two things that statement does not tell you.

Whether the API checks that the object in a request belongs to the caller, and whether a payment is limited to the payee and amount the user approved. The profile only recommends RAR. For the first it has one general clause (section 5.3.4: the resource server shall verify that the authorization the token represents is sufficient for the request), and it defines no per-object rule, so that check is the API's own code. It also says nothing about how each client stores its private key, or whether a user understood the consent screen.

Quick check

sections.html:
A stolen-token attack is already blocked. A token with scope payments:write, used by the real client, pays 9,000 EUR to an account the user never saw. Which control limits a token to the payment the user approved?

Exercises

sections.heading: Change one thing and predict the output
sections.heading_text: Change one thing and predict the output
sections.html:
Each exercise edits one place in labs/advanced_oauth_lab.py and asks what the run prints. The answers are the real output of each variant, not a reading of the code. The lab compares every result with the one it expects, so each of these edits makes it exit 1 and list what differed. All four need the cryptography package, as the lab does.

1. The server stops checking the assertion's audience

In AuthorizationServer._authenticate_assertion, delete the two lines that call self._audience_ok and return invalid_client: audience. Everything else, including the signature check, stays.

Which checks change?

Every option, and why
  • Check 12 does flip, and it is not alone. The issuer-only server in check 17 refuses its assertion for one reason, the audience, and that reason is the code this edit deletes.
  • Correct. Exit 1, two failures: checks 12 and 17 both go from invalid_client: audience to authenticated. Check 12 is an assertion ExamplePay signed for https://auth.other.example. Its signature is genuine, so nothing else refuses it. Any server that receives a client's assertion can now present it here, which is what check aoa-02 in the Reference layer asks you to rule out.
  • Check 16 already printed authenticated and still does. An edit that removes a refusal cannot change a check that was an acceptance.
  • The signature proves who made the assertion. It does not prove which server it was made for. Those are different claims, and aud is the only one that carries the second.

2. The request_uri is no longer bound to the client

In AuthorizationServer.authorize, delete the two lines that compare entry["client_id"] with the client making the request and return request_uri belongs to another client. The expiry and one-time-use checks stay.

What does the run print differently?

Every option, and why
  • Check 30 is right. Check 31 is the same request_uri, presented next by ExamplePay, and the one-time-use rule is still in force. The other client has just used it.
  • The server finds pushed requests by the request_uri alone. The value exists, so the lookup succeeds. The binding was a separate comparison, and it is the one that was deleted.
  • Correct. Exit 1, two failures. Check 30 goes from invalid_request: request_uri belongs to another client to code issued: a second client has started an authorization on ExamplePay's pushed request. Check 31 goes from code issued to invalid_request: request_uri already used: ExamplePay is locked out of its own request. RFC 9126 section 2.2 requires the binding, and check aoa-04 in the Reference layer tests for it.
  • Check 29 is a made-up value, which is still unknown to the server. It prints the same as before.

3. The API stops comparing the amount

In PaymentsAPI._covers, delete the line that compares d["instructedAmount"].get("amount") with body["amount"]. The creditor account and the currency are still compared.

Which checks change?

Every option, and why
  • Check 42 pays a different account, and the account is still compared. It still prints 403 Bearer error="insufficient_scope".
  • Correct. Exit 1, one failure: check 43 goes from 403 Bearer error="insufficient_scope" to 201 paid 450.00 EUR to acct-exampleair. The user approved 45.00 and the token still says 45.00. The API paid ten times that to the right payee, because one field of the granted object was no longer read. Check aoa-05 in the Reference layer says every field for this reason.
  • Check 44 runs against the API that checks only the type. It never compared the amount, so it already printed 201 and prints the same.
  • The authorization server validated the request and recorded 45.00. It is not present when the token is used. Only the resource server sees the payment that is actually submitted.

4. The step-up policy joins its two conditions with "and"

In PaymentsAPI.handle, the policy line reads if info["acr"] != ACR_MFA or age > PAYMENT_MAX_AGE:. Change or to and.

Which of the three challenged payments, checks 52, 56 and 57, still get a challenge?

Every option, and why
  • With and, a token is challenged only when it is both weak and old. Two of the three fail on one count only.
  • Check 56 is a second-factor sign-in from 30 minutes ago. Its acr is the required one, so the first half of the condition is false and the whole condition is false.
  • Correct. Exit 1, two failures: checks 56 and 57 both go from the insufficient_user_authentication challenge to 201 paid 45.00 EUR to acct-exampleair. Check 52, a password sign-in two hours old, fails on both counts and is still challenged. A test with only that one token would pass on the broken policy, which is why check aoa-07 in the Reference layer asks for a token that is old but strong and one that is fresh but weak.
  • Check 52 is weak and old, so even the loosened condition is true for it.

sections.heading: Controls
sections.html:
Standard backed by a cited specification. Baseline this project's default, with reasoning above. Option valid depending on the threat model.

  • StandardRFC 9700 section 2.5 recommends asymmetric cryptography for client authentication, such as mutual TLS (RFC 8705) or signed JWTs (private_key_jwt), and says authorization servers should enforce client authentication where issuing and protecting client credentials is feasible.
  • StandardThe client must not use more than one authentication method in a request. RFC 6749 section 2.3. The server must not rely on public client authentication to identify the client. Same section.
  • StandardA JWT used for client authentication must contain iss, sub equal to the client_id, an aud that identifies the authorization server, and exp, and must be signed or carry a MAC. The server must reject one with an invalid signature or MAC, one that does not name it as audience, and one that has expired. RFC 7523 section 3. Failures are reported as invalid_client. RFC 7523 section 3.2.
  • StandardRFC 7523 section 3 allows, and does not require, a jti claim and replay tracking. OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2, section 9, requires jti for private_key_jwt and client_secret_jwt and requires that the assertion be used only once unless the parties negotiated otherwise.
  • StandardFor JWT client authentication the client should use the authorization server's issuer identifier as the audience, and the server must accept its issuer identifier, its token endpoint URL or its PAR endpoint URL. RFC 9126 section 2.
  • StandardThe PAR endpoint must authenticate the client as the token endpoint does, must reject a pushed request that contains request_uri, and must validate the request as it would an authorization request. RFC 9126 section 2.1.
  • StandardThe request_uri must contain a part generated with a cryptographically strong pseudorandom algorithm so that guessing a valid value is computationally infeasible, and must be bound to the client that posted the request. RFC 9126 section 2.2.
  • StandardAn expired request_uri must be rejected. The server should treat request_uri values as one-time use and may allow a duplicate caused by a reload. The client must use a value only once. RFC 9126 section 4.
  • StandardServer policy may make PAR the only way to pass authorization request data, globally or per client, signalled by require_pushed_authorization_requests. The server then refuses other authorization requests with invalid_request. RFC 9126 sections 4, 5 and 6.
  • StandardThe server must accept new redirect URIs in a pushed request only from authenticated clients. RFC 9126 section 7.2. Clients should use PKCE, a unique state or the OpenID Connect nonce against request URI swapping. RFC 9126 section 7.5.
  • StandardEach authorization_details object requires a type. The server must refuse an unknown type, unknown fields, fields of the wrong type, invalid values and missing required fields, with invalid_authorization_details. RFC 9396 sections 2 and 5.
  • StandardThe token response must return the authorization_details as granted, and the authorization server must make them available to the resource server. RFC 9396 sections 7 and 9.
  • StandardIf the integrity of authorization_details is a concern, clients must protect them against tampering and swapping, with a signed request object or with PAR. The server must sanitize the data to prevent injection. RFC 9396 section 12.
  • StandardA resource server signals that the authentication behind a token is not sufficient with the error code insufficient_user_authentication, and may state the requirement with acr_values, max_age or both. RFC 9470 section 3. The client should use those values in a new authorization request. RFC 9470 section 4.
  • StandardThe authorization server should treat a requested acr as necessary when issuing the access token, and fail the request if it cannot be met. RFC 9470 section 5. RFC 9470 must not be used to position OAuth as an authentication protocol. RFC 9470 section 9.
  • StandardThe resource owner password credentials grant must not be used. RFC 9700 section 2.4. Clients should not use the implicit grant or other response types that return an access token in the authorization response, unless access token injection is prevented and the leakage vectors that section names are mitigated. RFC 9700 section 2.1.2.
  • StandardA client that can interact with more than one authorization server is required to have a defense against mix-up attacks, and should use the iss parameter of RFC 9207 or an equivalent issuer value in the response. RFC 9700 section 2.1. A client that supports RFC 9207 must compare iss with the issuer of the server the request was sent to and reject a mismatch. RFC 9207 section 2.4.
  • StandardUnder the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile, authorization servers shall authenticate clients with mutual TLS or private_key_jwt, shall reject authorization requests sent without PAR, shall require PKCE with S256, shall return iss, shall issue only sender-constrained access tokens, and shall reject the password grant. FAPI 2.0 Security Profile sections 5.3.2.1 and 5.3.2.2. Resource servers shall verify the token and that the authorization it represents is sufficient. Section 5.3.4.
  • BaselineRegister private_key_jwt for every confidential client. Accept one audience, the issuer identifier. Cap the assertion lifetime and record each jti until exp, after the signature and claims have passed.
  • BaselineTake the assertion's algorithm and key from the client's registration, never from the JWT header.
  • BaselineRequire PAR for every client whose request parameters matter. Use only what was pushed, and ignore anything else on the authorization URL.
  • BaselinePut anything with an amount, a payee or a named object in authorization_details. At the API, compare every field of the granted object with the request. Build the consent text from the same object.
  • BaselineValidate the token before applying the step-up policy, so that an invalid token is not told what the policy is.
  • BaselineTreat a profile claim as a list to verify row by row, and test object-level authorization separately.
  • OptionMutual TLS client authentication (tls_client_auth or self_signed_tls_client_auth, RFC 8705 section 2) where client certificates are already managed.
  • OptionA signed request object (RFC 9101), pushed through PAR, where the client must be able to prove afterwards what it requested.
  • OptionAdopt the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile whole, with a certified implementation, where an ecosystem or a regulator requires it.

sections.heading: Review checklist items
sections.html:
These are collected into the site checklist.

  • Confidential clients authenticate with a key the server cannot use The registered method is private_key_jwt or a mutual TLS method. Any client still on a shared secret is listed with what it can reach.
  • Client assertions are checked for signature, issuer, subject, one audience, expiry and single use Test an assertion made for another server, an expired one, one with a far exp, and the same one twice. The algorithm comes from the registration.
  • Pushed authorization requests are required, not just supported require_pushed_authorization_requests is set for the server or the client, and an authorization request with parameters on the URL is refused.
  • A request_uri is single use, short lived, unguessable and bound to its client Test a second use, a use after expires_in, a made-up value and a use with another client_id. Confirm the rightful client can still use it after the last one.
  • Transaction parameters are in authorization_details and the API enforces every field Test a payment that differs from the granted object in payee, in amount and in currency, one at a time. Each must be refused.
  • The authorization server refuses details it does not define or the client may not use Unknown types, unknown fields and missing fields get invalid_authorization_details. The client compares the token response with what it asked for.
  • Consequential operations check acr and auth_time and challenge when either falls short Test a token that is old but strong and one that is fresh but weak. Both get insufficient_user_authentication with the required acr_values and max_age.
  • No implicit or password grant is reachable, including by default Read grant_types_supported and each client's grant_types and response_types. Metadata that omits grant_types_supported defaults to including implicit.
  • Clients check the iss parameter of the authorization response A response whose iss is not the issuer the request went to is dropped before the code is redeemed. RFC 9700 requires a mix-up defense of any client that uses more than one authorization server.
  • A profile claim is not accepted as evidence of authorization With every control above in place, request an object that belongs to another customer. No control in the profile makes that check for the API. The API must refuse.

details.summary: A design says "the service uses the client credentials grant, so it authenticates with a client secret". What is wrong with the sentence?
details.html:
A design says "the service uses the client credentials grant, so it authenticates with a client secret". What is wrong with the sentence?

It treats two choices as one. The client credentials grant is how the client obtains a token. The client authentication method is how it proves which client it is, and any method can be used with that grant, including private_key_jwt and mutual TLS. Ask which method is registered, and what an attacker would need in order to use it.

details.summary: A server validates client assertions exactly as RFC 7523 section 3 requires. An attacker copies one assertion from a log 20 seconds after it was made. What happens?
details.html:
A server validates client assertions exactly as RFC 7523 section 3 requires. An attacker copies one assertion from a log 20 seconds after it was made. What happens?

It may well be accepted. RFC 7523 requires the signature, iss, sub, aud and exp checks, and the copy passes all of them until it expires. Tracking jti is optional in that RFC. OpenID Connect Core section 9 requires single use. Check 11 of the lab is the first server and check 10 is the second.

details.summary: An API returns 401 with error="insufficient_user_authentication" and max_age="300". The client refreshes its access token and retries. Does that work?
details.html:
An API returns 401 with error="insufficient_user_authentication" and max_age="300". The client refreshes its access token and retries. Does that work?

No. RFC 9470 section 6.1 says auth_time and acr are set when the user authenticates and do not change when a token is renewed. The client has to send the user through a new authorization request that carries max_age=300, so that the authorization server authenticates the user again.

details.summary: A vendor says its payments API is FAPI 2.0 certified. Name two things that statement does not tell you.
details.html:
A vendor says its payments API is FAPI 2.0 certified. Name two things that statement does not tell you.

Whether the API checks that the object in a request belongs to the caller, and whether a payment is limited to the payee and amount the user approved. The profile only recommends RAR. For the first it has one general clause (section 5.3.4: the resource server shall verify that the authorization the token represents is sufficient for the request), and it defines no per-object rule, so that check is the API's own code. It also says nothing about how each client stores its private key, or whether a user understood the consent screen.

Every option, and why
  • Check 12 does flip, and it is not alone. The issuer-only server in check 17 refuses its assertion for one reason, the audience, and that reason is the code this edit deletes.
  • Correct. Exit 1, two failures: checks 12 and 17 both go from invalid_client: audience to authenticated. Check 12 is an assertion ExamplePay signed for https://auth.other.example. Its signature is genuine, so nothing else refuses it. Any server that receives a client's assertion can now present it here, which is what check aoa-02 in the Reference layer asks you to rule out.
  • Check 16 already printed authenticated and still does. An edit that removes a refusal cannot change a check that was an acceptance.
  • The signature proves who made the assertion. It does not prove which server it was made for. Those are different claims, and aud is the only one that carries the second.

Every option, and why
  • Check 30 is right. Check 31 is the same request_uri, presented next by ExamplePay, and the one-time-use rule is still in force. The other client has just used it.
  • The server finds pushed requests by the request_uri alone. The value exists, so the lookup succeeds. The binding was a separate comparison, and it is the one that was deleted.
  • Correct. Exit 1, two failures. Check 30 goes from invalid_request: request_uri belongs to another client to code issued: a second client has started an authorization on ExamplePay's pushed request. Check 31 goes from code issued to invalid_request: request_uri already used: ExamplePay is locked out of its own request. RFC 9126 section 2.2 requires the binding, and check aoa-04 in the Reference layer tests for it.
  • Check 29 is a made-up value, which is still unknown to the server. It prints the same as before.

Every option, and why
  • Check 42 pays a different account, and the account is still compared. It still prints 403 Bearer error="insufficient_scope".
  • Correct. Exit 1, one failure: check 43 goes from 403 Bearer error="insufficient_scope" to 201 paid 450.00 EUR to acct-exampleair. The user approved 45.00 and the token still says 45.00. The API paid ten times that to the right payee, because one field of the granted object was no longer read. Check aoa-05 in the Reference layer says every field for this reason.
  • Check 44 runs against the API that checks only the type. It never compared the amount, so it already printed 201 and prints the same.
  • The authorization server validated the request and recorded 45.00. It is not present when the token is used. Only the resource server sees the payment that is actually submitted.

Every option, and why
  • With and, a token is challenged only when it is both weak and old. Two of the three fail on one count only.
  • Check 56 is a second-factor sign-in from 30 minutes ago. Its acr is the required one, so the first half of the condition is false and the whole condition is false.
  • Correct. Exit 1, two failures: checks 56 and 57 both go from the insufficient_user_authentication challenge to 201 paid 45.00 EUR to acct-exampleair. Check 52, a password sign-in two hours old, fails on both counts and is still challenged. A test with only that one token would pass on the broken policy, which is why check aoa-07 in the Reference layer asks for a token that is old but strong and one that is fresh but weak.
  • Check 52 is weak and old, so even the loosened condition is true for it.
